angle: A hype "level-up run" with one idea per level, built on draft B's structure and timing grid (5.0 / 9.5 / 12.0 / 12.5 / 12.5 / 3.5 = 55.0 s), with the judges' best lines grafted in. HOOK: one worker crawls the tasks one at a time, then all 320 go at once, then 'It scales… / then stalls.' LEVEL 1/3, ONE CPU: 'That worker? / One CPU core.' Then '16 cores. / 16 different jobs.' sharing one memory, and 'Need more?' LEVEL 2/3, ONE GPU: '16? Cute. / Meet the GPU.' Thousands of tiny cores work in groups of 32 on one instruction, doing the same math for every pixel. Then 'For AI? / Not enough.' LEVEL 3/3, DATA CENTER: many boxes with no shared memory pass messages. 'Go bigger.' leads into the film's biggest drop, '100,000+ / GPUs. One AI.', and then 'More GPUs…' plays over a riser that never resolves. Then the FINAL BOSS: a record-scratch glitch tears the counter away, and the twist runs 'So… infinite / speed?' → 'No.' → 'A million / GPUs?' → the curve stalls → '10% serial / = max 10×.' → 'Forever.' The ending asks 'Why buy / 100,000 GPUs?' and zooms back down to the one amber worker, which loops into frame 0. The SIMD, 8-GPU node and planet segments stay removed. Each scale opens from the previous one's token: worker → CPU core T6 → CPU token flips into the GPU → one box of the pod → cluster → serial block → worker.
logline: One amber worker levels up to 1,689,600,000+ CUDA cores working at once, and then the final boss, Amdahl's law, caps it at 10×.
counter_unit: CORES WORKING AT ONCE. It reads 'CORE WORKING AT ONCE' while the number is 1; measured at 6.06 wide singular and 6.38 plural, against a 6.9 limit. It climbs 1 → 16 → 16,896 → 1,689,600,000+ and never drops. Why it is honest: every number is a literal spec count of what the maker calls a core. 1 = the hook's worker, now one CPU core. 16 = a Ryzen 9 9950X (16 physical cores, not its 32 threads). 16,896 = the FP32 CUDA cores of one H100 SXM5 (132 SMs × 128). 1,689,600,000+ = 100,000+ H100s × 16,896. Why not 'CALCULATIONS AT ONCE': with SIMD cut, that unit forces either an untaught '× 16 lanes' (256) or a CPU value of 16. A 9950X core actually handles 16 FP32 numbers per AVX-512 instruction, so 16 would undercount the CPU about 16× and inflate the CPU-to-GPU jump by the same factor. That is a factual error; 'CUDA cores aren't real cores' is only a vocabulary quibble. How the CUDA-core pitfall is handled: each jump's LIME line names the kind of core ('16-CORE RYZEN 9 9950X', 'H100: 16,896 CUDA CORES', '100,000+ GPUs × 16,896'). The GPU cards qualify them before the number lands ('Thousands of / tiny cores.', then 'Groups of 32. / One instruction.'), set against the CPU's '16 different jobs.' The caption, logline and pinned comment never call the 1.69 billion 'cores' without 'CUDA'. No CPU-to-GPU ratio is ever shown, because it would read as a speed claim. The counter appears for the first time in the CPU segment. The twist's glitch tears it out by 0.30 s. A separately labelled SPEEDUP meter (1.0× → 10×, which also only climbs) enters 1.6 s later on 'No.', so a muted viewer never sees the counter drop.

caption: 1 worker → 16 CPU cores → 16,896 CUDA cores → 1.7 BILLION CUDA cores training ONE AI. Then the final boss shows up: if 10% of the job can't be split, you max out at 10× faster. Forever. So why buy 100,000 GPUs? Wrong answers only ↓
pinned_comment: How to beat the final boss: Gustafson's law (1988). Amdahl's 10× cap assumes the job stays the same size. AI labs grow the job with the machine (bigger models, more data), so the parallel part keeps growing and 100,000 GPUs still pay off. Nerd notes: a "CUDA core" is NVIDIA's name for one tiny FP32 math lane. They run 32 at a time on one instruction (a warp), so they are not CPU-style cores. H100 SXM5 = 132 SMs × 128 = 16,896. The CPU count is physical cores (a 9950X has 16 cores / 32 threads). The 10% serial share is just an example.
fact_notes: DURATIONS: hook 5.0 + CPU 9.5 + GPU 12.0 + data center 12.5 + twist 12.5 + ending 3.5 = 55.0 s (verified in Python). Every slot is a multiple of 0.5. Film cuts land at 5.0 / 14.5 / 26.5 / 39.0 / 51.5 / 55.0, so the ending still starts at 51.5 and its locked clock and f209 seam are unchanged. Every collapse is canonical motif.cut_times() output: CPU 8.933/9.333/9.45, GPU 11.433/11.833/11.95, data center and twist 11.933/12.333/12.45, hook 4.833/4.95. The biggest drop lands at film 33.88 s (61.6%).

'It scales… / then stalls.' measures at a full 84 px; the old 'until it doesn't.' was 17 chars and shrank to 69.6. '320 WORKERS · 1 STEP' is the ideal case, and the twist then shows the real-world limit (facts pitfall).

CPU: 'One CPU core' / '16 cores. 16 different jobs.' / LIME '16-CORE RYZEN 9 9950X' come from fact cpu_consumer_amd: Ryzen 9 9950X = 16 cores / 32 threads (phoronix.com/review/amd-zen5-avx-512-9950x). The counter counts physical cores, not threads. Naming the chip avoids the overgeneralisation in '1 CPU = 16 CORES': the most common PC has 8 cores and Intel's flagship has 24 (cpu_typical, cpu_consumer_intel). 'They share one memory.' is true for cores within one CPU (the dc_message_passing pitfall) and sets up 'No shared memory.' in the data center.

GPU: LIME 'H100: 16,896 CUDA CORES' comes from fact gpu_h100_sxm_fp32 (132 SMs × 128 FP32 CUDA cores, the SXM5 part; the PCIe card has 14,592). 'CUDA cores' is NVIDIA's own term. 'Thousands of tiny cores.' follows gpu_cuda_core_definition (FP32 lanes with no instruction fetch or scheduler of their own). 'Groups of 32. One instruction.' is the facts' safe phrasing for gpu_warp_size, with 'warps' replaced by the jargon-free 'groups'; 32 is NVIDIA-specific, AMD CDNA uses 64. 'Same math, every pixel.' is true because every pixel runs the same shader program, and the visual paints the image in scattered waves of groups, never in one instant (gpu_pixels pitfall). The old '66× ONE CPU' line is dropped, and no CPU-to-GPU ratio appears anywhere. 'For AI? Not enough.' rests on dc_meta_llama: frontier training uses 16K to 100K+ GPUs.

DATA CENTER: 'Many boxes. No shared memory.' and 'So they pass messages.' come from fact dc_message_passing: across nodes, GPUs sync over InfiniBand/Ethernet with collectives such as all-reduce (docs.nvidia.com/dgx/dgxb300-user-guide). '100,000+ / GPUs. One AI.' is the facts' own safe phrasing (dc_colossus1: '…GPUs. One AI.'), backed by xAI Colossus (100,000 H100s, 2024) and Meta's Llama 4 cluster (more than 100,000 H100s, Oct 2024). It uses the safe '100,000+' and never the unaudited 1M+ claims. 100,000 × 16,896 = 1,689,600,000 (verified), and the '+' matches '100,000+'. The 56×56 hall visual is representative.

TWIST: from fact amdahl_law, S(N) = 1/(0.1 + 0.9/N), checked in Python with motif.speedup_str's floor rounding. N=2 gives 1.818 → 1.8×; 4 gives 3.077 → 3.0×; 8 gives 4.706 → 4.7×; 16 gives 6.400 → 6.4×; 1,000,000 gives 9.99991 → 9.9×. '10×' appears only at 'GPUs: ∞', the limit, with the label 'MAX SPEEDUP · 10% SERIAL'. 'A million GPUs?' is posed as a hypothetical, not a claim about any real cluster. The 10% serial share is illustrative. 'Forever.' paraphrases the facts' safe phrasing '10% serial = max 10x. Forever.' and holds for a fixed-size job; the ending question and the pinned Gustafson comment (gustafson_law) cover the nuance that parallelism is not pointless.

ENDING: 'Why buy' replaces 'So why build' because labs buy GPUs and build clusters. It is true that xAI and Meta each bought 100,000+. It measures 67.1 px, the same as the current line, and cuts the question to 4 words, so question + CTA show 7 words. The loop clock, the f209 seam and the end frame ('PARALLEL COMPUTING' + 'One at a time.' + STEP 032 / 320) are unchanged.

COUNTER PATH: there is no HUD in the hook (the AMBER step readout is a separate element). The CPU opens at 1 → 16 (LIME at 3.70) → GPU 16,896 (LIME at 3.45) → data center 1,689,600,000+ (LIME at 7.383). The twist's glitch tears the counter out by 0.30, and the SPEEDUP meter (own label) enters at 1.90 and climbs 1.0× → 10×. Neither meter ever displays a smaller number in its own unit.
risks: USER DECISION, counter unit. I chose 'CORES WORKING AT ONCE' because every number is a literal spec count. The alternative, 'CALCULATIONS AT ONCE', which the virality judge preferred, would undercount the 9950X about 16× (one AVX-512 instruction handles 16 FP32 numbers per core) and inflate the CPU-to-GPU jump by the same factor, now that SIMD is cut. The cost of 'cores': expect 'CUDA cores aren't real cores' comments, softened on screen by 'tiny cores', 'Groups of 32. One instruction.' and the 'CUDA CORES' LIME line, and in the pinned nerd note. If you prefer CALCULATIONS anyway, the only text changes are the HUD label and the CPU LIME line, and that line must not claim '× 1 EACH'.

USER DECISION, the twist closer 'Forever.' One judge wanted a final punch before the ending question; another warned that a closer like 'Math wins.' reads as 'parallelism is pointless'. 'Forever.' is the facts file's own safe phrasing and stays scoped to '10% serial = max 10×'. The longer scoped line 'Even at ∞ GPUs.' fails card() (63.6 < 65 px). Fallback: drop 'Forever.' and hold the takeaway from 9.00 to 12.45.

USER DECISION, game framing. The kickers use 'LEVEL 1/3 · ONE CPU' … 'LEVEL 3/3 · DATA CENTER' and 'FINAL BOSS: AMDAHL'S LAW' (colon instead of ' · ', since the dot version fails the 6.9 width at tracking 80). Hype voice also shows in '16? Cute. / Meet the GPU.' and 'Go bigger.' If that reads as cringe, the text-only fallbacks are 'SCALE 1/3 · ONE CPU' … and the existing 'THE CATCH · AMDAHL'S LAW' (6.86 at 80), plus 'Now, a GPU.' in place of '16? Cute.'.

USER DECISION, pinned comment timing. The pinned comment gives away the Gustafson answer, which can deflate 'Wrong answers only ↓'. Consider posting it a few hours after upload, or pinning just the first sentence as a hint.

'Same math, / every pixel.' plays over a GPU whose stats are an H100, an AI chip with no display outputs, so a pedant may object. The kicker stays generic ('ONE GPU') and only the LIME line names the H100. Measured fallback: 'Same math, / every number.' (72.4 px).

Implementation is more than re-timing. (1) timeline.py: BEATS = B01 5.0 / B03 9.5 / B04 12.0 / B06 12.5 / B08 12.5 / B09 3.5, with B02Simd, B05Node and B07Planet removed from BEATS and ENERGY; b01 T_SWAP moves from 160 to 162 frames. (2) The motif.py handoff contract: E01 now opens into CPU hero T6 (keep HERO = 5). The E03 HUD becomes '16', and CALC_LABEL becomes 'CORES WORKING AT ONCE', with a singular 'CORE…' at 1. E04 opens into the data-center pod. E06 (cluster token + 1,689,600,000+ HUD) now feeds b08, whose opening glitch must tear both away, because b08 was written for a blank E07. Remove E02, E05 and E07 from _HO_TOKEN, _HO_HUD, BEAT_ENTRY and BEAT_EXIT, then re-run tools/check_handoffs.py at 30 and 60 fps. (3) b03: hide the 16 leftover SIMD lane bars per core, so nobody counts 256 lit lanes under a '16'. (4) b04: roll from 16 (not 256) and replace '66× ONE CPU' with the CUDA CORES line. b06: roll from 16,896 (not 135,168). (5) Text must hard-cut at t_exit, never fade.

Audio uses only instruments that already exist in audio/synth.py. The 'record scratch' is glitch + noise_burst. The never-resolving riser is a riser cut dead by the glitch. The heartbeat uses the existing lub/dub hits. No chime or vinyl sample is needed.

Tight floors that must POP or SLAM at full opacity (any fade-in frame breaks them): 'All at once.' 1.70/1.70, the CTA 1.72/1.7, 'No.' 1.15/1.1, takeaway 2.10/2.0, 'For AI?' 2.15/2.0, 'Some work' 2.40/2.3, 'Need more?' 1.55/1.4. Re-check them after any re-time.

C's bar labels '10% one at a time' / '90% all at once' were judged the best definition of serial, but they measure 3.95 + 3.46 wide against a 6.7-wide bar and would overlap. The script keeps the current '10% can't split' / '90% can split', which pass b08's ≥ 0.3 gap assert.

Undercount, never overclaim: the HUD holds 16,896 while the 64-box pod visibly computes (1.5-6.4 s in the data center), and it only rolls once the camera zooms out to the hall. Also, the hook's '320 WORKERS' readout is followed by a CPU HUD reading '1'. That is a different element, and 'That worker? / One CPU core.' frames it as zooming into one worker, but a viewer could read it as a step down.

Tail length: 21.1 s run from the biggest drop (film 33.88) to the loop seam. The twist has a text or visual event at least every ~1.2 s (glitch, bar, 'No.', cracks, whip, doublings, race, wall, takeaway, heartbeat, 'Forever.', launch). If analytics show drop-off there, the first lever is to trim the twist to 12.0 s and give the 0.5 s to the data center.

LIME 'H100: 16,896 CUDA CORES' auto-fits to 37.7 px, about 6% smaller than the other two LIME lines at 40. Every variant that keeps both 'H100' and 'CUDA CORES' is the same width or wider (measured 36.1-37.0). It passes the 34 px floor.
